egress.terms: Free - it is a shared filesystem (Gfarm), not a metered object store. Transfer via scp/rsync/GridFTP-style tools.

record.tooling: Gfarm 2.8 filesystem; mounted space, standard POSIX tools (rsync/rclone local backend).
record.chaining: A storage-only proposal: the 'Sharing Use' call exists precisely for projects that need shared space rather than compute time. Request 500 TB, then request gradual expansion to 1.5 PB based on usage.
record.limits_note: Requires an organisational representative's online approval at submission; project must specify a plan to remove data by project end. Annual/periodic calls; resource granted per project period, not perpetually.

record.reliability_note: Enterprise DDN + Gfarm, cross-hub replication. Stable. The binding constraint is the organisational sign-off and the end-of-project deletion requirement.

'Awarding result will be notified as soon as the screening process is completed. (Estimated to be within one or two weeks after a proposal is received.)', quoted

Trial Access screening method is 'Online application content confirmation and eligibility screening' for first-touch and 'Review of the application form and eligibility screening' for the 100,000 NH tier, against 'Expert screening' for General Access, quoted

Proposal instructions section 2: the general-category project representative is 'a person belonging to a legal entity (university, research institute, incorporated association, company, etc.) regardless of whether inside or outside Japan', except that company employees must belong to a company registered in Japan, quoted in Japanese

FAQ: use by non-residents of Japan and by non-Japanese nationals 'is possible'; a non-resident may be project representative; for Fugaku, projects with non-resident participants need separate R-CCS approval, quoted in Japanese

record.notes: The strongest single number in evaluated benchmarks: 100,000 Fugaku node-hours free, open all year, no competitive expert review at the trial tier. Fugaku nodes carry one A64FX CPU with 48 compute cores plus 4 assistant cores, so 100,000 node-hours is roughly 4.8 million core-hours; that conversion is arithmetic from the published node design, not a quoted figure. The binding door is the organisational signature, not money and not the science case. Foreign non-resident participants are explicitly allowed but require separate R-CCS approval under the Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Act.
